analysis.investment_thesis: Retaggio is a 2022-incorporated micro-cap jewellery maker (Mcap ~INR 88 Cr) with an ROE of just 0.12% and a P/E of 17x that has no meaningful earnings base to justify it. There is no track record, no compounding evidence, and no margin of safety — this fails every filter I apply.
key_strengths: Promoter holding is reasonable at 60.18%, giving skin-in-the-game
Debt-free-looking small balance sheet (inferable from size; to be verified)
Operates in jewellery, a consumer-facing category with cultural demand in India
key_risks: ROE of 0.12% is effectively zero — no demonstrated earning power
Only 3-year-old company with no long-term operating record or dividend history
Jewellery is working-capital heavy and hyper-competitive vs Titan/Kalyan/regional chains
red_flags: P/E of 17x on near-zero ROE implies earnings are trivial and the multiple is meaningless
Micro-cap BSE-listed jewellery SME — classic profile for price manipulation and poor liquidity
No visibility on governance, related-party transactions, or inventory quality at this size
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I built DMart by buying proven, cash-generating businesses at sensible prices and holding for decades. Retaggio fails the very first test: it has no history. Incorporated in 2022, listed as a micro-SME, and generating an ROE of 0.12% — that is not a business returning capital, that is a shell of activity. A P/E of 17x means nothing when the "E" is a rounding error; the number is cosmetic. In jewellery specifically, the capital cycle is brutal — gold inventory, making charges, receivables from wholesalers, hallmarking compliance — and only operators with decade-plus relationships (Titan, Kalyan, Senco, regional family chains) earn durable 15-18% ROE. A three-year-old 88-crore entity has no moat here.

Promoter holding at 60% is the only positive, and FII holding of 1.39% in a name this small is statistically noise, not conviction. For my framework — debt <0.3x, ROE >15%, consistent dividends, 10+ year track record, predictable consumer demand — this checks zero boxes. I would not touch it at any price until there is at least 5-7 years of audited, growing, cash-backed profitability. Score: 1/10. Avoid.
